title: Template identity matching versus the real speaker envelope
hypothesis: Choosing between the two original presets by median F0 is not a timbre decision: the LTAS distance between the presets is small compared with the distance from either preset to a real AISHELL speaker, so identity preservation must be defined against the mechanical input envelope, not against the real recording.

git.status: dirty at run time: parse_syllable fix, per-boundary evidence, align.py, new tests and EXP-0017/0018 records uncommitted

notes: Analysis only: no training, no template fitting, no new pairs. Reads the 16 usable pairs of EXP-0018 v3. Metric: level-normalised log-mel LTAS (24 bands, 100-7000 Hz), dB RMS. Result: the F0 heuristic matches the closer preset on 10/16 = 0.625 of pairs (operational claim supported), but median d(preset,preset)=6.03 dB versus median d(real,best preset)=6.92 dB, gap/separation 1.01 (pre-registered quantitative claim NOT supported). Five low-F0 speakers are closer to 'yang', i.e. F0 does not predict timbre. The 1-D formant-scale fit is not identifiable (7/16 pinned at the 1.30 edge, median 1.175). v1 (0.75-1.20 grid) kept as a failed artefact. Numeric pass/fail thresholds were written after the run and are labelled descriptive in the README.
